about.summary: I have 2 years of experience in 24x7 managed SOC (MSSP) and enterprise environments, investigating escalated, high-severity incidents from triage to scoping, containment, remediation and root cause analysis (RCA). I am strongest in **EDR investigation and detection engineering**, tuning SIEM rules mapped to MITRE ATT&CK to cut false positives and response time. Most recently I worked at the Department of Telecommunications T-SOC, supporting national-level threat response for ISPs.

experience.org: Department of Telecommunication UP East LSA (On Contractual Basis)

bullets.title: Threat Monitoring and National-Level Response
bullets.text: Monitor and mitigate threats to critical telecom networks in the TSOC; act on DoT Headquarters incident reports, helping ISPs validate IOCs, assess exposure, apply mitigations and report status.

bullets.title: Threat Intelligence and Advisory
bullets.text: Analyze malicious IPs, domains and attack patterns across ISPs; publish weekly Cyber Threat Advisories with IOCs, context and mitigation steps.

bullets.title: Detection Testing and Simulation
bullets.text: Built APT simulation labs and IR workflows to refine Wazuh SIEM detection rules.

bullets.title: ISP Security Auditing
bullets.text: Conducted Minimum Baseline Security Standard (MBSS) audits and vulnerability assessments for ISPs, reviewing controls, compliance and network architecture.

bullets.title: Alert Triage and Monitoring
bullets.text: Triaged and investigated 50+ alerts daily across Microsoft Sentinel, Rapid7 InsightIDR and Seceon while steadily cutting false positive escalations.

bullets.title: Incident Response
bullets.text: Handled High and Critical incidents end to end with a 15-minute initial response and a full report within 1 hour: scoped affected hosts and accounts, built attack timelines from SIEM and EDR data, coordinated containment and remediation with client IT teams, and documented impact and mitigation.

bullets.title: EDR Administration and Endpoint Analysis
bullets.text: Trained and worked as EDR Administrator on CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne and Cylance; managed policies and configuration, analyzed process trees, isolated hosts and stopped lateral movement.

bullets.title: Detection Engineering and Rule Tuning
bullets.text: Built and tuned SIEM detection and correlation rules mapped to MITRE ATT&CK (T1078 Valid Accounts, T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter, T1110 Brute Force); adjusted conditions, thresholds and exclusions, reducing alert noise by 30% through false positive tuning and closing detection gaps.

bullets.title: SOC Readiness and Documentation
bullets.text: Configured log source integrations, ran SIEM health checks and aligned detection coverage with client threat profiles and compliance needs; wrote SOPs, RCAs, runbooks and investigation notes.

bullets.title: DLP, CASB and SWG Analysis
bullets.text: Monitored Forcepoint DLP, CASB and SWG for a large enterprise client; investigated data-exfiltration, cloud, web and policy-violation events, and escalated confirmed incidents with evidence.

bullets.title: Vulnerability Management and Reporting
bullets.text: Prepared client vulnerability reports from scanner data (software, vendors, affected assets, patches) and compared them with the last two months to show trends, recurring exposures and remediation progress.

casework.intro: Real cases from my SOC work, with client details removed.

cases.title: Account renamed to “admin”
cases.text: An account was renamed to “admin” just before an administrative task, so the activity would look routine. Reviewing the account history showed it was already compromised.

cases.title: Forwarding rule after a VPN login
cases.text: A compromised Office account signed in through a low-cost VPN, then created a rule forwarding mail from the Deleted Items folder to an attacker-controlled address.

cases.title: One service on many hosts
cases.text: An attacker installed the same service on several hosts to move laterally. Process-creation events (event ID 4688) for that service across multiple hosts exposed it.

cases.title: Cutting false positives
cases.text: Scheduled-task alerts fired on legitimate tasks from vendors such as Google and Microsoft, and macOS login failures came from the akd service. I added exclusions so analysts saw fewer false positives.
